source_text: Desine itaque impiare te (si tamen ullum tibi fas aut nefas restat), Christi verba sic exponendo, ut ille arbitrium negasse liberum videatur, sine cuius integritate aequitas ei proprii non potest constare iudicii.
pass_a_gloss: Cease therefore to make yourself impious (if nevertheless any fas or nefas remains for you), by so expounding the words of Christ, that he seem to have denied free choice, without whose integrity the equity of his own judgment cannot stand for him.

lemmas.lexica: LS arbitrium=judgment, free decision; Blaise liberum arbitrium
LS liber=free; Blaise unde liberum est abstinere

pass_b_english: Stop making yourself impious, then, if any distinction between right and wrong still remains for you, by explaining Christ's words as though he had denied free choice. Without that choice remaining intact, the fairness of his own judgment cannot stand.

choices.why: Glossary default: arbitrium is the decision-power, not a later Augustinian/Reformation free-will locus.
Freedom to abstain is required for will and sin.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
